==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/tɹeɪs/|[tʃɹeɪs]|q2=sometimes}} * {{audio|en|en-us-trace.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-trace.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪs|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|trace}}, {{m|enm|traas}}, from {{der|en|fro|trace|t=an outline, track, trace}}, from the verb (see below). ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # An [[act]] of [[#Verb|tracing]]. #: {{ux|en|Your cell phone company can put a '''trace''' on your line.}} # An [[enquiry]] sent out for a [[missing]] [[article]], such as a letter or an express package. # A [[mark]] left as a [[sign]] of [[passage]] of a [[person]] or [[animal]]. #: {{syn|en|track|trail}} # A very [[small]] [[amount]], often [[residual]], of some [[substance]] or [[material]]. #: {{syn|en|show}} #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:modicum}} #: {{ux|en|There are '''traces''' of chocolate around your lips.}} #: {{ux|en|All of our chocolates may contain '''traces''' of nuts.}} ## {{lb|en|meteorology}} A small amount of [[rain]], not enough to be [[measure]]d. #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=7|passage=The highway to the East Coast which ran through the borough of Ebbfield had always been a main road and even now, despite the vast garages, the pylons and the gaily painted factory glasshouses which had sprung up beside it, there still remained an occasional '''trace''' of past cultures.}} #* {{quote-song|en|author=w:Taylor Swift;w:Imogen Heap|authorlabel=no|title={{w|Clean (song)|Clean (Taylor's Version)}}|album=w:1989 (Taylor's Version)|date=27 October 2014|date_published=27 October 2023|artist=Taylor Swift|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RKAXdSe8MYM|text=And by mornin'
Gone was any '''trace''' of you, I think I am finally clean}} # {{lb|en|electronics}} A [[current]]-[[carry]]ing [[conductive]] [[pathway]] on a [[printed circuit board]]. # An [[informal]] [[road]] or [[prominent]] [[path]] in an [[arid]] [[area]]. # One of two [[strap]]s, [[chain]]s, or [[rope]]s of a [[harness]], extending from the [[collar]] or [[breastplate]] to a [[whippletree]] attached to a [[vehicle]] or thing to be drawn; a [[tug]]. # {{lb|en|engineering}} A connecting [[bar]] or [[rod]], [[pivot]]ed at each [[end]] to the end of another [[piece]], for [[transmit]]ting [[motion]], especially from one [[plane]] to another; specifically, such a piece in an [[organ stop]] action to transmit motion from the [[trundle]] to the [[lever]] actuating the stop slider. # {{lb|en|fortification}} The [[ground plan]] of a [[work]] or works. # {{lb|en|geometry}} The [[intersection]] of a [[plane]] of [[projection]], or an original plane, with a [[coordinate]] plane. # {{sid|en|Q321102}} {{lb|en|linear algebra}} The sum of the [[diagonal]] elements of a square [[matrix]]. # {{lb|en|grammar}} An [[empty]] [[category]] occupying a position in the [[syntactic]] [[structure]] from which something has been moved, used to explain [[construction]]s such as [[wh-movement]] and the [[passive]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Georges Rebuschi; Laurice Tuller|title=The Grammar of Focus|page=290 |passage=[S]upposing the NP has raised in (18), the potential bindees are the clitic and the '''trace''' of the focalized NP, neither of which qualifies as a syntactic variable.}} # {{lb|en|programming}} A [[sequence]] of [[instruction]]s, including [[branch]]es but not [[loop]]s, that is executed for some [[input]] [[data]]. # {{lb|en|semiotics}} A {{senseid|en|adj-small}} Extremely small or [[insignificant]] (of an amount or [[quantity]]). #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2025|author=Aoun, Joseph |journal=The Status of Movement Rules|passage=As indicated in Chomsky (1982), the empty element in (26a) has an antecedent with an independent 0-role and is therefore PRO rather than '''trace'''. Subjacency is violated, but nevertheless PRO and its antecedent can be coindexed, as is generally possible for anaphors, apart from trace (in (26c), the coindexing of ''they'' and ''each other'' violates subjacency). In (26b), the antecedent of the empty element is in a non-0-position, so the empty element is '''trace'''. Subjacency is violated as in (26a), but in this case, the sentence is ungrammatical.⁹ Thus subjacency appears to be a property of the rule Move α, not of other indexing mechanisms. If this conclusion is correct, then clearly we will have to distinguish between the indexing mechanism at work in (25a) or (26b) -- i.e. Move α -- and the one at work in (25b-c) or (26a,c).}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|trace element}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|tracen}}, from {{der|en|fro|tracer}}, {{m|fro|trasser||to delineate, score, trace", also, "to follow, pursue}}, probably a conflation of {{der|en|la-vul|*tractiō||to delineate, score, trace}}, from {{der|en|la|trahere||to draw}}; and Old French {{m|fro|traquer||to chase, hunt, pursue}}, from {{m|fro|trac||a track, trace}}, from {{der|en|dum|treck}}, {{m|dum|treke||a drawing, draft, delineation, feature, expedition}}. More at {{l|en|track}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To follow the [[trail]] of. #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=9|passage=I feel thy power {{...}} to '''trace''' the ways / Of highest agents.|year=1873}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1792|author=w:William Cowper|title=On a Similar Occasion for the Year 1792 |passage=Happy the mortal, who has '''traced''' effects
To their first cause}} # To follow the history of. #* '''1684-1690''', {{w|Thomas Burnet}}, ''Sacred Theory of the Earth'' # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[draw]] or [[sketch]] lightly or with care. #: {{ux|en|He carefully '''traced''' the outlines of the old building before him.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To copy onto a sheet of paper superimposed over the original, by drawing over its lines. # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To copy; to imitate. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1647|author={{w|John Denham (poet)|John Denham}}|title=To Sir Richard Fanshaw |passage=That servile path thou nobly dost decline, / Of '''tracing''' word by word, and line by line.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[walk]]; to [[go]]; to [[travel]]. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=VI|canto=III|stanza=29|passage=Not wont on foote with heavy armes to '''trace'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To walk over; to pass through; to traverse. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing|III|i|passage=We do '''trace''' this alley up and down.}} # {{lbl|en|computer|transitive}} To follow the execution of the program by making it to stop after every instruction, or by making it print a message after every step. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|backtrace|mistrace|overtrace|traceability|traceable|traceback|tracee|untrace|test and trace|track and trace| trace down|trace out}} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|tracing}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to follow the trail of}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Latin: * Māori: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Spanish: * Thai: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to follow the history of}} * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * Hungarian: * Malay: * Māori: * Spanish: * Thai: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to draw or sketch}} * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Finnish: * French: * Hungarian: * Portuguese: * Spanish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to copy onto a sheet of superimposed paper}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Hungarian: * Ido: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Spanish: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|''(obsolete in English)'' to copy;
